finding.claim: The /fetch handler passes the user-supplied `target` query parameter straight to http.Get with no validation. An attacker can make the server request internal or cloud-metadata addresses, such as http://169.254.169.254/ or http://localhost:*. The response body is copied back to the attacker, so this is full-read SSRF.
finding.sink: http.Get(target), with the response body written to the client via io.Copy

trace.note: Route /fetch is registered to the fetch handler
target is read from the query string
http.Get(target) issues the server-side request to the attacker-chosen URL
The upstream response body is returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: There is no scheme, host or IP check, no allowlist and no private-range blocking. The `allowed` map is used only by safeFetch, not by fetch. Redirects are followed by default. Authentication is absent.

verdict.reason: main.go:15-16 reads `target` from the query string and passes it to http.Get unvalidated, main.go:22 copies the response body back, main.go:41 registers /fetch to this handler, and the `allowed` check exists only in safeFetch (main.go:27).
